name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to accounts when passwords or other credentials are unknown.

name: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries may systematically guess passwords to obtain valid credentials for accounts on a target system.

name: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries may attempt a small number of commonly used passwords against many accounts to avoid account lockouts.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit vulnerabilities in Internet-facing software (e.g., SQL injection, command injection) to gain access.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to discover active remote services and accessible open ports across network segments (port scanning).

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing legitimate accounts to gain access and maintain persistence.

name: Default Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse default or factory-configured credentials on applications and network devices.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries may steal and transmit sensitive data back to an external command and control server.

name: Exfiltration Over Physical or High-Volume Medium
description: Adversaries may exfiltrate bulk enterprise data through large outbound network streams or external channels.

name: Automated Exfiltration
description: Adversaries may use automated transfer scripts and agents to exfiltrate collected sensitive records.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters (Bash, Python, PowerShell) to execute commands.

name: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell environments to execute arbitrary scripts and interactive commands.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries may create an account on a system to maintain access to target resources.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in elevated processes or kernel routines to elevate privileges.

name: Sudo and Sudo Caching
description: Adversaries may abuse sudo permissions and caching mechanisms to run unauthorized commands with root privileges.

name: Active Scanning
description: Adversaries may execute active reconnaissance scans to probe network services and perimeter defenses.

name: Vulnerability Scanning
description: Adversaries may scan web applications and perimeter hosts using automated tools to identify unpatched flaws.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may dump credentials from the operating system security subsystems and memory.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware configuration.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries may communicate using standard application layer protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend into legitimate traffic.

name: Web Protocols
description: Adversaries may communicate using standard HTTP/HTTPS channels to control remote implants.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised network.

name: Masquerading
description: Adversaries may disguise artifacts, files, or user agents to mimic legitimate software or users.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling mechanisms like cron to facilitate ongoing execution.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with malicious links or attachments to gain access.
